note: Human-authored historical validation cases (WO-010 Gate J). Each case states what was known at its own assessment cutoff, what the platform is expected to conclude, and the hindsight limitation that applies. scripts/build_events_from_cases.py deterministically expands these into data/events/*.json, and scripts/run_historical_validation.py replays them through the platform's own analysis code and asserts every expectation. Evidence content was NOT retrieved under WO-010 -- no source was reachable from the execution environment -- so every evidence item carries evidence_class 'historical_validation_fixture', retains the publisher's original URL for verification, and records that limitation explicitly. Later knowledge must not leak into a case's cutoff: each case's facts_known_at_cutoff is the whole factual basis its expectations may rely on.

event.title: Container carriers divert Asia–Europe services away from the Red Sea and Suez routing
thailand_relevance_basis: Thailand westbound container services to Northern Europe and the Mediterranean normally transit Bab el-Mandeb and the Suez Canal, so a routing change on that corridor lengthens the Thailand lanes that use it.
The relationship is a lane-transit relationship, not a Thailand-specific event: nothing here establishes an effect on any particular Thailand service or shipper.

transmission_chain.external_driver: Security risk to merchant shipping in the southern Red Sea and Gulf of Aden.
transmission_chain.operational_change: Carriers rerouted Asia–Europe services around the Cape of Good Hope instead of transiting Bab el-Mandeb and Suez.
transmission_chain.logistics_mechanism: A longer routing absorbs more vessel days per round trip, which withdraws effective capacity from the service string and shifts arrival schedules.
transmission_chain.observable_indicator: Published carrier service advisories, Suez Canal transit counts, and container freight benchmarks for Asia–Europe routings.
transmission_chain.outcome: Observed increase in transit time on affected Asia–Europe strings, with potential cost and capacity effects on Thailand lanes routed through the same corridor.

evidence.claim: The canal authority publishes monthly transit statistics against which a decline in transits during the diversion period can be checked.
Public reporting during December 2023 described multiple container carriers suspending Red Sea transits and rerouting via the Cape of Good Hope.

known_limitations: Not assessed for this area at the case cutoff; this is a gap, not a finding of no impact.

transmission_mechanism: Diversion around the Cape of Good Hope lengthens the routing and adds vessel days per round trip.
known_limitations: Transit-time effect is established for the corridor, not measured for any individual Thailand service.

transmission_mechanism: Longer round trips shift published arrival schedules and degrade schedule reliability on affected strings.
known_limitations: Schedule reliability is not measured by any source qualified in this registry.

transmission_mechanism: Absorbing additional vessel days on the same fleet withdraws effective capacity from the trade.
known_limitations: Capacity withdrawal is inferred from routing length; no deployed-capacity series is qualified in this registry.

transmission_mechanism: Reduced effective capacity and higher fuel consumption per voyage exert upward pressure on freight benchmarks for affected routings.
known_limitations: No Thailand-origin freight rate source is qualified, so no Thailand cost effect is quantified anywhere.

transmission_mechanism: Longer transit on Thailand westbound lanes shifts delivery timing for goods moving to European markets.
known_limitations: No Thailand trade series was retrieved to confirm a flow effect.

facts_known_at_cutoff: Multiple container carriers had publicly announced suspension of Red Sea transits and rerouting via the Cape of Good Hope.
The Suez Canal Authority publishes transit statistics that would show a decline.
Thailand westbound container lanes to Northern Europe and the Mediterranean normally use this corridor.
expectations.hindsight_limitation: The duration of the diversion, its eventual freight-rate peak and its effect on Thailand trade volumes were all unknown at this cutoff and must not inform the assessment.

event.title: Panama Canal Authority restricts daily transit slots during drought conditions
thailand_relevance_basis: The Panama Canal is a routing option for Asia to United States East and Gulf Coast services, which is one Thailand lane.

Whether any given Thailand service actually routes via Panama rather than Suez is carrier-specific and is not published by any source qualified in this registry, so exposure is potential rather than confirmed.

transmission_chain.external_driver: Prolonged drought reduced the water available to operate the canal's lock system.
transmission_chain.operational_change: The canal authority reduced the number of daily transit slots and applied draft restrictions.
transmission_chain.logistics_mechanism: Fewer slots force waiting, slot auctions, or rerouting via Suez or the United States West Coast, each of which changes transit time or cost.
transmission_chain.observable_indicator: Canal authority advisories stating the slot count and draft limit.
transmission_chain.outcome: Potential transit-time and cost effects on Thailand services routed to the United States East and Gulf Coast via Panama.

evidence.claim: The canal authority published advisories to shipping setting a reduced number of daily transit slots and a maximum authorised draft during drought conditions.

known_limitations: Not assessed for this area at the case cutoff; this is a gap, not a finding of no impact.

transmission_mechanism: Reduced daily slots force waiting or rerouting for services that transit the canal.
known_limitations: Which Thailand services transit Panama is not published by any qualified source, so exposure is unconfirmed.

transmission_mechanism: Slot scarcity raises the cost of securing a transit, whether through auction premiums or a longer alternative routing.
known_limitations: No Thailand-origin freight rate source is qualified; no Thailand cost effect is quantified.

facts_known_at_cutoff: The canal authority had published advisories reducing daily transit slots and applying draft restrictions.
The restriction is a published operating condition of the waterway, not a report about any individual carrier.
expectations.hindsight_limitation: How long the restrictions lasted, and whether slot counts were later restored, was unknown at this cutoff.

event.title: Francis Scott Key Bridge collapse suspends vessel traffic at the Port of Baltimore

transmission_chain.operational_change: Vessel traffic into and out of the Port of Baltimore was suspended after the bridge collapse blocked the channel.
transmission_chain.logistics_mechanism: A closed channel removes a port from the service rotation and forces cargo to alternative United States East Coast gateways.
transmission_chain.observable_indicator: Port and coastguard notices, and port call counts for Baltimore and neighbouring East Coast ports.
transmission_chain.outcome: Observed suspension of Baltimore vessel traffic. No Thailand lane effect is established, because no evidence links Thailand ocean cargo to this port.

evidence.claim: The port administration announced that vessel traffic into and out of the Port of Baltimore was suspended until further notice following the bridge collapse.

known_limitations: No evidence links Thailand ocean cargo to the Port of Baltimore. The correct answer is insufficient evidence, not no impact: the platform has not assessed and disproved a Thailand effect, it has found no basis to assess one.

facts_known_at_cutoff: The port administration had suspended vessel traffic at Baltimore.
Baltimore is a United States East Coast port with no service relationship to Thailand recorded in this platform's reference data.
expectations.hindsight_limitation: The channel reopening timetable and the eventual cargo diversion pattern were unknown at this cutoff. This case exists to check that a large, well-reported event with no established Thailand link produces 'insufficient evidence' rather than an invented transmission chain.

event.title: Elevated vessel waiting times reported at Singapore container terminals
thailand_relevance_basis: Singapore is the principal transshipment hub for Thailand long-haul ocean services, so waiting time at Singapore transmits to Thailand cargo through the transshipment leg.
The transmission is through transshipment connection times, not through any direct Thailand port condition.

transmission_chain.operational_change: Vessel waiting times before berthing at Singapore container terminals rose above their normal range.
transmission_chain.logistics_mechanism: Longer waiting before berthing delays discharge and reloading of transshipment boxes, which extends connection times for cargo relayed through the hub.
transmission_chain.observable_indicator: Port authority operational notices reporting waiting time, and berth occupancy measures.
transmission_chain.outcome: Observed capacity pressure at the hub, with potential service effects on Thailand cargo transshipped through it.

evidence.source_name: Maritime and Port Authority of Singapore
evidence.claim: The port authority published operational guidance addressing elevated vessel waiting times and the additional berth capacity brought into service to relieve them.
Estimated port call counts at Singapore remained at or above their prior range during the period.

known_limitations: Not assessed for this area at the case cutoff; this is a gap, not a finding of no impact.

transmission_mechanism: Elevated waiting time before berthing reduces effective berth throughput at the hub.
known_limitations: Supported by an operational-condition notice from the port authority. Port call counts alone would not have supported this conclusion: throughput measures how much moved, not how long anything waited.

transmission_mechanism: Delayed discharge and reloading at the hub extends transshipment connection times for relayed Thailand cargo.
known_limitations: No transshipment connection-time series is qualified in this registry, so the Thailand-side effect is potential rather than measured.

facts_known_at_cutoff: The port authority had published operational guidance addressing elevated vessel waiting times.
Estimated port call counts had not fallen, so the pressure was not visible in volume data.
Singapore is the principal transshipment hub for Thailand long-haul services.
expectations.hindsight_limitation: How long the elevated waiting times persisted, and whether they spread to neighbouring hubs, was unknown at this cutoff. This case exists to check that a congestion conclusion requires an operational-condition source and is never derived from throughput alone.

event.title: Crude and refined product prices rise sharply, raising bunker and domestic fuel costs
thailand_relevance_basis: Thailand imports refined product and prices domestic diesel against international benchmarks, so an international energy shock transmits into domestic transport cost.
Bunker fuel is a direct input to ocean freight cost on every Thailand lane.

transmission_chain.external_driver: A sharp rise in international crude and refined product prices.
transmission_chain.operational_change: Bunker fuel and domestic diesel prices rose alongside the international benchmark.
transmission_chain.logistics_mechanism: Bunker cost is a direct input to ocean freight pricing and is commonly recovered through bunker surcharges; domestic diesel is a direct input to inland drayage cost.
transmission_chain.observable_indicator: Published crude benchmarks and Thailand retail diesel prices.
transmission_chain.outcome: Potential cost pressure across Thailand ocean lanes and the domestic port connection, with no measured effect on any Thailand shipment price.

evidence.source_name: Energy Policy and Planning Office, Thailand
evidence.claim: The energy office publishes Thailand retail fuel prices, against which a domestic pass-through of an international price movement can be checked.

known_limitations: Not assessed for this area at the case cutoff; this is a gap, not a finding of no impact.

transmission_mechanism: Higher bunker prices raise the fuel component of ocean freight cost and are commonly recovered through bunker surcharges.
Higher domestic diesel prices raise inland drayage cost between Thailand ports and the hinterland.
known_limitations: Pass-through from a crude benchmark to a bunker price, and from a bunker price to a freight rate, is neither immediate nor proportional. No Thailand freight rate source is qualified, so no cost effect is quantified.

transmission_mechanism: Sustained high bunker cost can prompt slow steaming, which lengthens transit time.
known_limitations: Whether carriers actually adjusted service speed is not established by any qualified source.

facts_known_at_cutoff: International crude and refined product prices had risen sharply.
Thailand publishes retail fuel prices that track international benchmarks with a lag.
expectations.hindsight_limitation: The eventual peak and duration of the price movement were unknown at this cutoff. This case exists to check that an external driver with a complete chain produces potential cost pressure rather than a quantified cost figure.

event.title: Damage to Baltic Sea subsea telecommunications cables reported

transmission_chain.external_driver: Reported damage to subsea telecommunications cables in the Baltic Sea and the associated security investigation.

evidence.claim: Public reporting in November 2024 described damage to subsea telecommunications cables in the Baltic Sea and an associated security investigation.

known_limitations: No operational change to any port, service or routing has been established, so no Logistics transmission mechanism can be stated and the item remains contextual.
Supported only by discovery-class evidence, which can never be the sole basis for a material impact conclusion.

facts_known_at_cutoff: Public reporting described damage to subsea telecommunications cables and an associated investigation.
No port, terminal, canal or carrier had announced any operational change.
expectations.hindsight_limitation: This case exists to check that a widely reported security event with no stated Logistics mechanism stays contextual, produces no impact conclusion, and is not admitted to any lane assessment. Whether a mechanism was later established is irrelevant to the assessment at this cutoff.

event.title: Pasir Panjang oil spill response with port operations reported unaffected
event.operator_or_entity: Maritime and Port Authority of Singapore
thailand_relevance_basis: Singapore is Thailand's principal transshipment hub, so a port event there is assessed for a Thailand transshipment effect even when none is found.

transmission_chain.operational_change: An oil spill response was mounted near Pasir Panjang Terminal.
transmission_chain.logistics_mechanism: A spill response can restrict navigation or berthing, which would delay vessel calls and transshipment connections.
transmission_chain.observable_indicator: Port authority notices stating whether navigation and berthing were restricted.
transmission_chain.outcome: The operator stated that navigational traffic and berthing operations were not affected, so no material logistics impact was detected.

event.closure_basis: The operating authority stated that navigation and berthing were unaffected, and no subsequent notice reported an operational restriction.

evidence.source_name: Maritime and Port Authority of Singapore
evidence.claim: The operating authority stated that navigational traffic and berthing operations at Pasir Panjang Terminal were not affected at the time of the notice.

known_limitations: The finding rests on the operating authority's own statement at the time of the notice and covers logistics operations only. Environmental and recreational effects are outside this conclusion.

facts_known_at_cutoff: An oil spill response was underway near the terminal.
The operating authority explicitly stated that navigation and berthing were not affected.
expectations.hindsight_limitation: This case exists to check the one legitimate use of 'no material impact detected': an actual assessment against explicit negative operational evidence, never an unassessed area.

event.title: Unverified report of a labour dispute affecting a Southeast Asian container terminal

evidence.claim: A discovery-class lead referring to a possible labour dispute at an unnamed Southeast Asian container terminal. No operating authority or carrier has published anything corresponding to it.

known_limitations: A discovery lead with no primary-source confirmation. It is displayed so that a reader can see what the platform is watching, and it supports no conclusion of any kind.

facts_known_at_cutoff: A discovery source surfaced a lead. Nothing else is known.
No terminal, port authority or carrier has published a corresponding notice.
expectations.hindsight_limitation: This case exists to check that a discovery lead is representable, visible, and structurally unable to support a conclusion.

event.title: Pakistan closes its airspace and Thailand–Europe air services are cancelled or rerouted
thailand_relevance_basis: Thailand–Europe air services depart from the registered Thailand air cargo gateway and their routing crosses the closed airspace, so the closure acts directly on a registered Thailand air lane.
The relationship is a lane-transit and gateway relationship. Nothing here establishes an effect on any particular Thailand shipment, shipper or cargo category.

transmission_chain.external_driver: A military-security escalation between two South Asian states.
transmission_chain.operational_change: The civil aviation authority closed its national airspace to civil traffic, and services on the Thailand–Europe air corridor whose routing crosses it were cancelled or rerouted around it.
transmission_chain.logistics_mechanism: Air cargo on this corridor moves substantially in the belly holds of scheduled passenger widebodies, so cancelling those services withdraws cargo capacity from the corridor; a rerouting that avoids the closed airspace lengthens the sector, which raises block hours and fuel burn per rotation and shifts published arrival times.
transmission_chain.observable_indicator: Operator service announcements, the airspace authority's own restriction notices, and air freight rate benchmarks for Asia–Europe routings.
transmission_chain.outcome: Observed cancellation and rerouting of Thailand–Europe air services, with capacity and cost consequences that are stated as mechanisms and are not measured anywhere in this platform.

evidence.claim: The civil aviation authority issued a notice to airmen on 27 February 2019 closing Pakistan airspace to civil traffic until further notice.

The operator announced on 27 and 28 February 2019 that Bangkok–Europe services whose routing crosses the closed airspace were cancelled, naming TG916 Bangkok–London, TG926 Bangkok–Phuket–Frankfurt and TG974 Bangkok–Moscow among them, and stated subsequently that a subset would resume on a rerouting cleared through Chinese airspace.
A Thai government agency published an update on 28 February 2019 recording that Thailand–Europe flights were affected by the Pakistani airspace closure.
Public reporting on 28 February 2019 described the Bangkok–Europe cancellations and the wider disruption to Asia–Europe air routings caused by the airspace closure.

known_limitations: Not assessed for this area at the case cutoff; this is a gap, not a finding of no impact.

Lane relevance resolved through the shared Thailand gateway node is a registry-membership relationship. It records that the lanes share a node with this event, not that an effect on those lanes was established.

transmission_mechanism: Services on the Thailand–Europe air corridor were cancelled outright or rerouted around the closed airspace on a longer sector.
known_limitations: Established from the operator's own service announcement for named flights. No corridor-wide movement or routing series is qualified in this registry, so the extent beyond the named services is not measured.

transmission_mechanism: A cancelled or lengthened sector shifts published arrival times and breaks the connection windows a shipment booked against.
known_limitations: Air schedule reliability is not measured by any source qualified in this registry.

transmission_mechanism: Cargo on this corridor moves substantially in the belly holds of the cancelled passenger widebodies, so withdrawing those services withdraws cargo capacity from the corridor.
known_limitations: The capacity withdrawal is a stated mechanism, not a measured quantity. No air cargo capacity, tonnage or movement series is qualified in this registry, and none was used to produce this reading.

transmission_mechanism: Withdrawn capacity and longer routings on the same fleet exert upward pressure on air freight rates for the affected corridor.
known_limitations: No free Thailand-scoped air freight rate benchmark exists, so no air cost effect is quantified anywhere in this platform. FBX_PUBLIC covers named east-west container routes only and cannot stand in for an air reading.

transmission_mechanism: Cancelled and lengthened Thailand–Europe air sectors shift delivery timing for the time-sensitive goods that move by air rather than by sea.
known_limitations: No Thailand air trade series was retrieved, so no flow effect is confirmed.

facts_known_at_cutoff: The civil aviation authority had closed its national airspace to civil traffic on 27 February 2019.
The operator had publicly cancelled named Bangkok–Europe services because their routing crosses that airspace, and had stated that a subset would resume on a rerouting through Chinese airspace.
A Thai government agency had published that Thailand–Europe flights were affected.
The registered Thailand–Europe air lane records that its routing crosses South Asian airspace.
expectations.hindsight_limitation: How long the closure would last -- it ran until 15 July 2019 -- and its eventual effect on air freight rates and on Thailand trade volumes were all unknown at this cutoff and must not inform the assessment. This case exists to check that the Air foundation carries a real event end to end: that an airspace closure resolves to an Air lane through the airspace chokepoint that lane actually records and to no Ocean lane at all, and that the capacity and cost consequences -- for which no Air series is qualified anywhere -- stay 'potential' with the gap named rather than being quantified from a source the platform does not hold.

event.title: Malaysia's Movement Control Order closes the Thailand–Malaysia land border to general movement while goods traffic continues
thailand_relevance_basis: The order closed the Malaysian side of a border corridor this platform registers and on which a Thailand road lane is anchored.
The relationship is corridor-transit and node membership. Nothing here establishes an effect on any particular Thai shipment or shipper.

transmission_chain.external_driver: A national public-health emergency order in Malaysia.
transmission_chain.operational_change: The border closed to general movement of persons and vehicles while goods traffic continued at designated checkpoints under reduced staffing.
transmission_chain.logistics_mechanism: Reduced staffing and restricted hours lengthen clearance at a single corridor through which Thailand–Malaysia road freight is funnelled, and the driver-exchange and escort arrangements imposed on goods vehicles add handling steps per crossing.
transmission_chain.observable_indicator: The border agencies' own operating notices and crossing-level throughput.
transmission_chain.outcome: Observed restriction of movement at the corridor, with freight-flow and cost consequences stated as mechanisms and measured nowhere in this platform.

evidence.claim: The Prime Minister announced on 16 March 2020 a Movement Control Order effective 18-31 March 2020, closing the country's borders to inbound and outbound movement of persons, with essential services exempt.
Customs operations at ports, airports and land entry points continued under the order with reduced staffing, and movement of goods continued at designated checkpoints including Bukit Kayu Hitam.
Public reporting on 23 March 2020 described all Thailand–Malaysia border checkpoints as closed to general crossing under the Movement Control Order.

known_limitations: Not assessed for this area at the case cutoff; this is a gap, not a finding of no impact.

Lane relevance resolved through shared country membership is a registry-membership relationship. It records that lanes share a country with this event, not that an effect on those lanes was established.

transmission_mechanism: The corridor closed to general movement while goods traffic continued at designated checkpoints under reduced staffing.
known_limitations: This event must never be read as a stoppage of freight across this corridor; goods movement was expressly exempted and no freight volume effect is measured by this platform.

transmission_mechanism: Reduced staffing and driver-exchange/escort arrangements at the crossing add handling steps and lengthen clearance time per vehicle.
known_limitations: Crossing-level clearance time is not measured by any source qualified in this registry.

transmission_mechanism: Reduced staffing and additional per-vehicle handling steps at a single corridor reduce the effective throughput available to Thailand–Malaysia road freight.
known_limitations: The capacity reduction is a stated mechanism, not a measured quantity. No road or border crossing capacity series is qualified in this registry, and none was used to produce this reading.

transmission_mechanism: Longer clearance times and additional handling steps at the crossing can exert upward pressure on road freight rates for the corridor.
known_limitations: No Thailand-origin road freight rate source is qualified, so no Thailand cost effect is quantified anywhere in this platform.

transmission_mechanism: Restricted movement at the corridor can shift delivery timing for goods moving by road between Thailand and Malaysia, even though goods movement itself was exempted from the order.
known_limitations: No Thailand road or border trade series was retrieved, so no flow effect is confirmed. This event must never be read as a stoppage of freight across this corridor.

facts_known_at_cutoff: The Prime Minister of Malaysia had announced a Movement Control Order effective 18-31 March 2020, closing the country's borders to general movement of persons.
Customs and border agencies had stated that goods movement continued at designated checkpoints, including Bukit Kayu Hitam, under reduced staffing.
Public reporting described Thailand–Malaysia border checkpoints as closed to general crossing.
expectations.hindsight_limitation: How long the restriction would last, and that on 17 June 2020 Malaysia ended 24-hour operations at Bukit Kayu Hitam for heavy vehicles, were both unknown at this cutoff and must not inform the assessment. This case exists to prove two things: that a border closure is not a freight stoppage -- goods movement was expressly exempted, so import_export must never be read as observed collapse -- and that mode scoping holds for Land: this event carries country_ids ['TH','MY'], which every Ocean lane touching Malaysia also carries, yet tagged modes ['road','border'] it must resolve no Ocean lane and no Air lane at all.
